matches.quote: Reversing polarity moves the main dissipation site by only ~80 nm (gate vs island), which is negligible on the µm scale probed. So polarity independence at µm scale cannot discriminate injection-type mechanisms
The NV readout uses green laser illumination and microwave pulses... Both can generate quasiparticles and heat locally, and could alter the threshold or the vortex configuration.
Contrary to "only weak correlation," r₀ is monotonic and steep in V_G within each temperature dataset. The datasets are merely offset, likely due to V_G drift.
Scans take substantial time while P fluctuates (e.g., 1.74(14) µW). The relation between the quoted P and the instantaneous suppression during image acquisition should be clarified.
No information is given on cooling history (field-cooled vs zero-field-cooled), reversibility (do vortices re-enter when P is removed?), statistics
r₀ is monotonic and steep in V_G within each temperature dataset. The datasets are merely offset, likely due to V_G drift.
The location, nature and stability of the current path (surface conduction, bulk oxide, filament formation, path through intrinsic Si) are not determined.
Laser and microwave powers, duty cycles, and controls (e.g., r₀ versus laser power) are not reported.
The substrate diffusion coefficient uses a room-temperature thermal diffusivity of glass (Ref. 29). At sub-Kelvin temperatures, amorphous SiO₂ has drastically different conductivity and heat capacity
The NV readout uses green laser illumination and microwave pulses from an adjacent CPW, about 100 nm above a superconductor at 0.4 K. Both can generate quasiparticles and heat locally
Contrary to "only weak correlation," r₀ is monotonic and steep in V_G within each temperature dataset. The datasets are merely offset, likely due to V_G drift.
Sub-100-nm determinations of r₀ (Fig. 3a error bars) are thus strongly model-dependent... Systematic uncertainties are not quantified.

notes: For C28, both the referee and P15 challenge the authors' claim that polarity independence rules out carrier injection, though via different physical arguments (hole equivalence vs 80 nm shift of the dissipation site). For C4, the review body text under P23 explicitly notes that the green readout laser could alter the vortex configuration. For C8 and C6, P18 identifies the same two offset steep curves in Fig. 3b but attributes the offset between temperature datasets to VG drift rather than a temperature effect.
